messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.

# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

{ "returncode": 0, "output_head": "# Chat bots Bots are chat members that post messages over HTTP. Scripts and CI jobs use them to report into rooms (`curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" https://chat.example.com/rooms///messages`). This document records the decisions behind the feature, so that changes to it start from the same understanding. ## How it fits together - **Bots are users.** `Bot < User`, a single-table-inheritance subclass stored in the `users` table (`users.type = 'Bot'`). Memberships, message authorship, avatars, mentions, unread tracking and push notifications all key off `User`, so bots reuse them without any special cases. - **Owner:** `users.creator_id` is the person who created the bot. `User has_many :bots`. - **Credential:** `users.bot_key` is the bot code: 32 random alphanumeric characters, unique, and shown on the bots page. It's the only thing the API checks. - **Password:** `users.password_digest` is NOT NULL, so each bot gets a random, unshared password digest. Bots never sign in, and have no email address, so they can't. - **Management UI:** `BotsController` (`/bots`, `/bots/new`, `/bots/:id/edit`). Reached from the bot icon on `/account/edit`, which every member sees. - **Posting API:** `Bots::MessagesController`, `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`. - **Webhooks:** an optional webhook URL. Campfire POSTs each mention of the bot to it, and the bot can answer in the response. See [Webhooks](#webhooks). ## Lifecycle - **Create:** a new bot joins every open room, the same as a new person (`User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms`). Bots can be added to closed rooms through the room forms, like people. - **Who manages a bot:** the creator, and administrators. The bots page lists the caller's own bots, or every bot for an administrator. Anyone else's bot is a 404, not a 403, so its existence isn't revealed. - **Delete:** `Bot#deactivate` is "delete". It removes the bot from every room (including direct rooms), sets `status: deactivated`, and clears `bot_key` and `webhook_url`. Its past messages stay, as they do for deactivated people. A deleted bot's code is a 401. - **Creator leaves or is banned:** `User#deactivate` and `User::Bannable#ban` deactivate the creator's bots. A bot shouldn't outlive the person it's acting for. Unbanning doesn't restore bots. ## Posting API `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` | Case | Response | | --- | --- | | Posted | `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:id` | | Empty or whitespace-only body, no attachment | `422 Unprocessable Content` | | Unknown, or deleted bot's code | `401 Unauthorized` | | Room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member | `404 Not Found` | - The raw body is the message text. No envelope, no field names. Text is stored as plain text: markup is escaped, and line breaks are kept. - Attachments use a multipart upload: an `attachment` file, with optional text in a `body` field. - Messages are created with `creator: bot` by `Bot#post_message`, which then runs `broadcast_create`. Masking it would mean filtering the SQL log, or encrypting the column with ActiveRecord encryption (which needs keys). - **Reverse proxies and access logs** record the request path, including the code. Operators should filter `/rooms/*/*/messages` out of proxy logs. - **Lookup:** `Bot.active.find_by(bot_key:)`, the same shape as session token lookup. ## Where bots appear | Surface | Bots? | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | Room member pickers (open and closed room forms) | yes | "Bots can be added to other rooms the same way as people." | | Messages, avatars, room member lists | yes | They're users. | | Mention autocomplete inside a room | yes | They're room members. | | Account people list (`/account/edit`), admin people list | no | Managed at `/bots`. `User.humans` excludes them. | | Direct message placeholders, ping autocomplete, direct room creation | no | A bot can't read a conversation, so pinging one is meaningless. | | Bot profile page (`/users/:id`) | yes, without ping, transfer or ban | Ping would create a direct room with only you in it. | `User.humans` is `where(type: nil)`. Use `where.not(type: "Bot")` with care: it drops NULL types in SQL. ## Known gaps and follow-ups - **`Location` points at a route that 404s for GET.** `/messages/:id` is the top-level message route, which `MessagesController` only uses for nested boosts. Its `show` runs the room-scoped `set_room`, so it 404s. Room-scoped `/rooms/:room_id/messages/:id` works. The spec fixes `Location`, so it's left as-is. A permalink redirect (top-level show → `room_at_message_path`) would fix it. - **No code rotation.** Regenerating a bot code means deleting the bot and creating a new one. Adding a "regenerate code" action would be a `bot_key` reset plus a confirm. - **Bot messages can only be edited or deleted by administrators,** not the bot's creator, since authorship is the bot. Widen `Current.user.can_administer?(message)` if creators should be able to moderate their bots. - **No rate limiting** on the posting endpoint. A leaked code can post freely until it's deleted. - **No size limit:** nothing caps the message size on the posting API beyond the server's own request limits. Webhook replies are capped at 64 KB. - **Webhook requests aren't signed.** A bot can't verify that a call came from Campfire. An unguessable path in the webhook URL is the only check for now. An HMAC header would need a per-bot secret. - **No delivery log or retries.** A failed call only shows in the server log, so a bot's author can't see why a reply didn't appear. - **Replies keep mention attachments.** An HTML reply can mention people the way a person's message can, so a bot can ping room members. Plain text replies never ping anyone. - **No rate limiting on webhook calls.** Each mention calls the webhook, and nothing throttles that. - **Event types:** only `mention` exists. ## Testing

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    trigger_bot_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    # Bots only answer people. A bot's own messages never call webhooks, so two bots can't set each other off.
    def trigger_bot_webhooks_later(message)
      return if message.creator.bot?

      message.mentioned_bots.each do |bot|
        Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, message)
      end
    end
end

# Rooms for direct message chats between users. These act as a singleton, so a single set of users will

class Rooms::Direct < Room
  class << self
    def find_or_create_for(users)
      find_for(users) || create_for({}, users: users)
    end

      def find_for(users)

require "net/http"
require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Calls a bot's webhook to say that someone mentioned it, then posts the bot's answer into the room, if it gave one.
#
# This runs in a background job, so the person who posted the mention never waits on it. Redirects aren't followed,
# and the webhook's host is resolved and checked against private networks before connecting, as link unfurling is.
# A bot's answer becomes a message, so only a 200 with a text body counts, and it's limited in size.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  class ReplyTooLargeError < StandardError; end

  attr_reader :bot, :message
  delegate :room, to: :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot, @message = bot, message
  end

  def deliver
    return unless deliverable?

    reply = request_reply
    post_reply(reply) if reply
  end

  private
    # The bot may have been removed from the room, deactivated or lost its webhook since the mention was posted.
    def deliverable?
      bot.active? && bot.webhook_url.present? && bot.rooms.exists?(room.id)
    end

    def request_reply
      reply = nil

      connect do |http|
        http.request(build_request) do |response|
          reply = read_reply(response) if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)
        end
      end

      reply
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.warn "Failed to call the webhook for bot #{bot.id} about message #{message.id} (#{e.class}: #{e.message})"
      nil
    end

    def connect(&)
      uri = webhook_uri
      ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(uri.host)

      Net::HTTP.start uri.host, uri.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
        open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, &
    end

    def build_request
      Net::HTTP::Post.new(webhook_uri.request_uri, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request|
        request.body = payload.to_json
      end
    end

    def read_reply(response)
      content_type = response.content_type&.downcase
      return unless REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(content_type)

      body = String.new
      response.read_body do |chunk|
        body << chunk
        raise ReplyTooLargeError if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE
      end

      { content_type: content_type, text: decode(body, response.type_params["charset"]) }
    end

    def decode(bytes, charset)
      encoding = Encoding.find(charset) rescue Encoding::UTF_8
      bytes.force_encoding(encoding).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace).scrub
    end

    def post_reply(reply)
      text = reply[:text].strip
      body = reply[:content_type] == "text/html" ? sanitized_html(text) : Bot.html_from_plain_text(text)

      return if body.blank? || ActionText::Content.new(body).to_plain_text.blank?

      bot.post_message(room, body: body)
    end

    def payload
      {
        event: "mention",
        author: { id: message.creator.id, name: message.creator.name },
        room: { id: room.id, name: room.name, reply_to: routes.bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key) },
        message: {
          id: message.id,
          body: { text: text, html: html },
          link: routes.room_at_message_path(room, message)
        }
      }
    end

    # The mention of the bot itself is removed, so the text reads as the command addressed to the bot.
    def text
      without_own_mention = message.body.body.fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node|
        node unless ActionText::Attachable.from_node(node) == bot
      end

      ActionText::Content.new(without_own_mention, canonicalize: false).to_plain_text.gsub(/[ \t]{2,}/, " ").strip
    end

    # A bot's HTML comes from outside Campfire, so it's sanitized the same way as a displayed body before it's stored.
    def sanitized_html(html)
      ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(ActionText::Content.new(html)).to_html
    end

    # The whole rich text body, sanitized the same way as when it's displayed. The bot's own mention stays in it.
    def html
      ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(message.body.body).to_html
    end

    def webhook_uri
      URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    end

    def routes
      Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
    end
end

class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  rescue_from(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound) { head :not_found }

  before_action :set_bot
  before_action :set_room

  def create
    if message_text.blank? && attachment.blank?
      head :unprocessable_content
    else
      message = @bot.post_message(@room, body: Bot.html_from_plain_text(message_text), attachment: attachment)

      head :created, location: message_path(message)
    end
  end

  private
    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: params[:bot_key])
      head :unauthorized unless @bot
    end

    # Bots only get rooms they're members of. Rooms they aren't in look just like rooms that don't exist.
    def set_room
      @room = @bot.rooms.find(params[:room_id])
    end

    # A raw body is the message. Attachments need multipart uploads, so their text comes from a body field instead.
    def message_text
      @message_text ||= begin
        text = multipart? ? params[:body] : request.raw_post
        text.is_a?(String) ? text.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub.strip : ""
      end
    end

    def multipart?
      request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
    end

    def attachment
      params[:attachment] if params[:attachment].is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)
    end
end

class RoomsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ destroy ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show

  def index
    redirect_to room_url(Current.user.rooms.last)
  end

  def show
    @messages = find_messages
  end

  def destroy
    @room.destroy

    broadcast_remove_room
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_room
      if room = room_scope.find_by(id: params[:room_id] || params[:id])
        @room = room
      else
        redirect_to root_url, alert: "Room not found or inaccessible"
      end
    end

    # Subclasses narrow this to the room types they're allowed to act on, so that one
    # room namespace can't be used to reach another's rooms.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@room)
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_create_rooms
      if Current.account.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators? && !Current.user.administrator?
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def find_messages
      messages = @room.messages.with_creator.with_attachment_details.with_boosts

      if show_first_message = messages.find_by(id: params[:message_id])
        @messages = messages.page_around(show_first_message)
      else
        @messages = messages.last_page
      end
    end

    def room_params
      params.require(:room).permit(:name)
    end

    def broadcast_remove_room
      broadcast_remove_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ]
    end
end

class RoomsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ destroy ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show

  def index
    redirect_to room_url(Current.user.rooms.last)
  end

  def show
    @messages = find_messages
  end

  def destroy
    @room.destroy

    broadcast_remove_room
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_room
      if room = room_scope.find_by(id: params[:room_id] || params[:id])
        @room = room
      else
        redirect_to root_url, alert: "Room not found or inaccessible"
      end
    end

    # Subclasses narrow this to the room types they're allowed to act on, so that one
    # room namespace can't be used to reach another's rooms.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@room)
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_create_rooms
      if Current.account.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators? && !Current.user.administrator?
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def find_messages
      messages = @room.messages.with_creator.with_attachment_details.with_boosts

      if show_first_message = messages.find_by(id: params[:message_id])
        @messages = messages.page_around(show_first_message)
      else
        @messages = messages.last_page
      end
    end

    def room_params
      params.require(:room).permit(:name)
    end

    def broadcast_remove_room
      broadcast_remove_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ]
    end
end

  end

  def sound

  end

require "test_helper"

class BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @creator = users(:david)
  end

  test "creating a bot gives it a bot code and an unguessable password it never uses" do
    bot = create_bot

    assert_match(/\A[[:alnum:]]{32}\z/, bot.bot_key)
    assert bot.password_digest.present?
    assert_nil bot.email_address
  end

  test "bot codes are unique" do
    bot = create_bot
    duplicate = Bot.new(name: "Copycat", creator: @creator, bot_key: bot.bot_key)

    assert_not duplicate.valid?
    assert duplicate.errors[:bot_key].any?
  end

  test "bot names are required" do
    bot = Bot.new(name: "", creator: @creator)

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert bot.errors[:name].any?
  end

  test "creating a bot grants it membership to the open rooms but not to closed rooms" do
    closed_room = rooms(:designers)
    closed_room.update!(type: "Rooms::Closed")

    bot = create_bot

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.rooms.opens.count
    assert_not bot.rooms.include?(closed_room)
  end

  test "bots are listed as the creator's bots" do
    bot = create_bot

    assert_includes @creator.bots, bot
    assert_not_includes users(:jason).bots, bot
  end

  test "bots are left out of the people scope" do
    bot = create_bot

    assert_includes User.all, bot
    assert_not_includes User.humans, bot
    assert_includes User.humans, users(:david)
  end

  test "deactivating a bot removes it from its rooms, clears its code and keeps its messages" do
    bot = create_bot
    message = rooms(:watercooler).messages.create!(creator: bot, body: "Deploy finished")
    old_code = bot.bot_key

    bot.deactivate

    assert bot.reload.deactivated?
    assert_nil bot.bot_key
    assert_equal 0, bot.memberships.count
    assert_equal bot, message.reload.creator
    assert_not Bot.active.exists?(bot.id)
    assert_nil Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: old_code)
  end

  test "bots know they are bots" do
    assert create_bot.bot?
    assert_not users(:david).bot?
  end

  test "deactivating a user deactivates the bots they created" do
    bot = create_bot
    other_bot = create_bot(creator: users(:jason))

    users(:david).deactivate

    assert bot.reload.deactivated?
    assert other_bot.reload.active?
  end

  test "banning a user deactivates the bots they created" do
    bot = create_bot

    users(:david).ban

    assert bot.reload.deactivated?
  end

  test "webhook URLs are optional, and a blank one removes the webhook" do
    bot = create_bot
    assert_nil bot.webhook_url

    bot.update! webhook_url: "https://bot.example.com/hook "
    assert_equal "https://bot.example.com/hook", bot.reload.webhook_url

    bot.update! webhook_url: "  "
    assert_nil bot.reload.webhook_url
  end

  test "webhook URLs must be HTTP or HTTPS URLs" do
    bot = create_bot

    [ "bot.example.com", "ftp://example.com/hook", "javascript:alert(1)", "https://", "not a url" ].each do |url|
      bot.webhook_url = url

      assert_not bot.valid?, "expected #{url.inspect} to be rejected"
      assert bot.errors[:webhook_url].any?
    end
  end

  test "only bots with a webhook URL are in the with_webhook scope" do
    with_webhook = create_bot
    with_webhook.update! webhook_url: "https://bot.example.com/hook"
    create_bot

    assert_equal [ with_webhook ], Bot.with_webhook.to_a
  end

  test "deactivating a bot clears its webhook" do
    bot = create_bot
    bot.update! webhook_url: "https://bot.example.com/hook"

    bot.deactivate

    assert_nil bot.reload.webhook_url
  end

  private
    def create_bot(creator: @creator)
      Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: creator)
    end
end
"

    class << self

  # Each bot that has just become a member gets a `joined` event. Called with the users whose memberships were
  # created by granting, so it fires once per room a bot joins. Direct rooms are private conversations, so they never
  # announce anyone. The jobs wait for the surrounding transaction to commit, so the webhook sees the new membership.
  def announce_bots_joined(user_ids)
    return if direct? || user_ids.empty?

    Bot.active.with_webhook.where(id: user_ids).each do |bot|
      ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit { Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, self) }
    end
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

# Calls a bot's webhook to say that someone mentioned it, then posts the bot's answer into the room, if it gave one.
#
# This runs in a background job, so the person who posted the mention never waits on it. Redirects aren't followed,
# and the webhook's host is resolved and checked against private networks before connecting, as link unfurling is.
# A bot's answer becomes a message, so only a 200 with a text body counts, and it's limited in size.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  class ReplyTooLargeError < StandardError; end

  attr_reader :bot, :message
  delegate :room, to: :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot, @message = bot, message
  end
EOF

# and the webhook's host is resolved and checked against private networks before connecting, as link unfurling is.
# A bot's answer becomes a message, so only a 200 with a text body counts, and it's limited in size.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  class ReplyTooLargeError < StandardError; end

  attr_reader :bot, :message, :room

  # A mention is about the message that made it. A join has no message, only the room the bot has joined.
  def initialize(bot:, message: nil, room: message&.room)
    @bot, @message, @room = bot, message, room
  end

class Bot::WebhookJob < ApplicationJob
  # If the bot or the message is gone by the time the job runs, there's nothing left to deliver.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  # The subject is the message that mentioned the bot, or the room the bot has just joined.
  def perform(bot, subject)
    case subject
    when Message then Bot::Webhook.new(bot: bot, message: subject).deliver
    when Room then Bot::Webhook.new(bot: bot, room: subject).deliver
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Room::BotJoinsTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  setup do
    @room = rooms(:designers)
    @bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://bot.example.com/hook")
  end

  test "a bot added to a room by a person gets one joined event for that room" do
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)
    end

    assert_enqueued_with job: Bot::WebhookJob, args: [ @bot, @room ]
  end

  test "a bot added through the room form gets one joined event for each room it's added to" do
    other_room = rooms(:watercooler)

    assert_enqueued_jobs 2, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @room.memberships.revise(granted: @bot)
      other_room.memberships.revise(granted: @bot)
    end
  end

  test "a bot is announced once, even when it's granted the room again" do
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)
      @room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)
      @room.memberships.revise(granted: @bot)
    end
  end

  test "a bot already in an open room isn't announced again when the room is re-opened" do
    room = rooms(:pets)
    room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)
    end
  end

  test "people joining a room don't get joined events" do
    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to([ users(:kevin), users(:jason) ])
    end
  end

  test "a bot without a webhook is added to the room without a joined event" do
    quiet_bot = Bot.create!(name: "Quiet Bot", creator: users(:david))

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to(quiet_bot)
    end
    assert @room.users.include?(quiet_bot)
  end

  test "a deactivated bot doesn't get a joined event" do
    @bot.deactivate

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)
    end
  end

  test "a bot put in a direct room gets no joined event, since direct conversations are private" do
    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      Rooms::Direct.create_for({ creator: users(:david) }, users: [ users(:david), @bot ])
    end
  end

  test "turning the switch on announces the bot once for each open room it joins" do
    assert_enqueued_jobs Rooms::Open.count, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @bot.update! add_to_all_open_rooms: true
    end

    assert_enqueued_with job: Bot::WebhookJob, args: [ @bot, rooms(:hq) ]
    assert_enqueued_with job: Bot::WebhookJob, args: [ @bot, rooms(:pets) ]
  end

  test "turning the switch on again doesn't announce the bot again" do
    @bot.update! add_to_all_open_rooms: true

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @bot.update! add_to_all_open_rooms: false
      @bot.update! add_to_all_open_rooms: true
    end
  end

  test "a new open room announces each bot that asked for every open room, once" do
    @bot.update! add_to_all_open_rooms: true
    other_bot = Bot.create!(name: "Build Bot", creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://build.example.com/hook")

    room = nil
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      room = Rooms::Open.create_for({ name: "Brand new", creator: users(:david) }, users: users(:david))
    end

    assert_enqueued_with job: Bot::WebhookJob, args: [ @bot, room ]
    assert_not_includes enqueued_jobs(only: Bot::WebhookJob).map { |job| job[:args] }.flatten.map(&:to_s), other_bot.to_global_id.to_s
  end

  test "a closed room that becomes open announces the bots that asked for every open room" do
    @bot.update! add_to_all_open_rooms: true

    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      @room.becomes!(Rooms::Open).update!(name: @room.name)
    end
  end

  test "the joined event is queued only once the membership has been committed" do
    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      @room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)

      assert_empty enqueued_jobs(only: Bot::WebhookJob)
    end

    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob
  end
end
EOF

require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Calls a bot's webhook to say that someone mentioned it, or that it has just joined a room, then posts the bot's answer
# into the room, if it gave one.
#
# This runs in a background job, so the person who posted the mention never waits on it. Redirects aren't followed,
# and the webhook's host is resolved and checked against private networks before connecting, as link unfurling is.
# A bot's answer becomes a message, so only a 200 with a text body counts, and it's limited in size.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  class ReplyTooLargeError < StandardError; end

  attr_reader :bot, :message, :room

  # A mention is about the message that made it. A join has no message, only the room the bot has joined.
  def initialize(bot:, message: nil, room: message&.room)
    @bot, @message, @room = bot, message, room
  end

  def deliver
    return unless deliverable?

    reply = request_reply
    post_reply(reply) if reply
  end

  private
    # The bot may have been removed from the room, deactivated or lost its webhook since the mention was posted.
    def deliverable?
      bot.active? && bot.webhook_url.present? && bot.rooms.exists?(room.id)
    end

    def request_reply
      reply = nil

      connect do |http|
        http.request(build_request) do |response|
          reply = read_reply(response) if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)
        end
      end

      reply
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.warn "Failed to call the webhook for bot #{bot.id} about #{subject_description} (#{e.class}: #{e.message})"
      nil
    end

    def connect(&)
      uri = webhook_uri
      ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(uri.host)

      Net::HTTP.start uri.host, uri.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
        open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, &
    end

"
}

## Open rooms

Bots don't join open rooms by default. People do: every active person is in every open room, and that doesn't change.
A bot is in an open room only if its author turned on **Add to all open rooms** on the bot form, which is a switch
(`users.add_to_all_open_rooms`, off by default).

- **Switch on:** the bot joins every open room that exists at that moment. This happens in `Bot#join_open_rooms`,
  from an `after_save` that only fires when the value changes, so saving the form again doesn't re-run it.
- **Rooms that appear later:** `Rooms::Open` grants a new open room to `User.joining_open_rooms`: every active person,
  plus the bots with the switch on. A closed room that becomes open gets the same grant, so it covers both new rooms
  and rooms converted to open.
- **Switch off:** the flag is cleared, but nothing else changes. The bot keeps every membership it has. There's no
  bulk leave.
- **Closed rooms** aren't affected by the switch. A bot gets into one only when a person picks it in the room form.
- **Deleting** a bot clears the switch along with its code and webhook.

Why a flag and not a one-off join: a switch that's on has to keep covering rooms created later, so the setting
has to be stored. The column lives on `users` because `Bot < User` is single-table inheritance. Only bots read it,
and it's false for everyone else.

cat > /tmp/n1 <<'EOF'
- A reply is an ordinary message from the bot. It's broadcast and queues push notifications like any other.
- Replies work the same for `joined` as for `mention`. The reply is posted into the room the bot joined.

### Joins

When a bot is added to a room, its webhook receives a `joined` event, once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/<bot-code>/messages" }
}
```

The payload has no author, message or body. The room is the same `room` object as in a mention, so the bot can
post into it straight away with `reply_to`, or answer in the response, the same as for a mention.

- **Which joins count:** any time a bot gains a membership in a room that isn't a direct room. That's the bot being
  added by a person (a closed room created or revised with the bot picked, or an open room the bot is put in by
  the switch), or automatically (a new open room, a room that becomes open, or the switch turned on).
- **Once per room:** a bot is announced only for memberships that were actually created. Granting a bot a room it's
  already in, or turning the switch on again, doesn't announce it again. A bot that leaves a room and is added back is
  a new join, so it's announced again.
- **Direct rooms never announce.** A direct conversation is private, so a bot never learns about it.
- **Bots without a webhook** aren't announced, since there's nowhere to send the event.
- **Queued after commit:** the event is enqueued after the surrounding transaction commits, so the webhook sees the
  membership when it runs. `Room::Memberships#grant_to` reports which memberships it created, using
  `insert_all(..., returning:)`. Only those rows are announced.
- **Removed before it runs:** `Bot::Webhook` checks the bot is still a member, active and has its webhook. A bot that
  has left the room isn't called, and a deactivated bot isn't called either.

**Every way a person or an automatic rule puts a bot in a room must go through `Room::Memberships#grant_to`.**
`insert_all` skips callbacks, so a row written any other way (for example `Membership.create!`) doesn't announce the
bot. In the app today that's `grant_to` (`Room.create_for`, `revise`, `Rooms::Open`) and `Bot#join_open_rooms`.
Tests that set up a bot's rooms with `memberships.create!` won't see a `joined` event, which is deliberate: those tests
are about something else.

### Limits and safety
EOF

require "ferrum"

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:3100"
browser = Ferrum::Browser.new(browser_path: "/usr/bin/chromium", headless: true, timeout: 30,
  browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-gpu" => nil, "disable-dev-shm-usage" => nil })

def switch_state(browser)
  browser.evaluate(<<~JS)
    (() => {
      const label = [...document.querySelectorAll("label")].find(l => l.textContent.trim().includes("Add to all open rooms"));
      if (!label) return { found: false };
      const cb = label.querySelector("input[type=checkbox]");
      const sw = label.querySelector(".switch").getBoundingClientRect();
      return { found: true, nested_checkbox: !!cb, checked: cb.checked, name: cb.name, id: cb.id,
               label_for_attr: label.getAttribute("for"), switch_w: Math.round(sw.width), switch_h: Math.round(sw.height) };
    })()
  JS
end

begin
  browser.goto("#{BASE}/session/new")
  browser.at_css("input[name=email_address]").type("david@example.com")
  browser.at_css("input[name=password]").type("secret123456")
  browser.at_css("button[type=submit], input[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  puts "after login: #{browser.current_url}"

  browser.goto("#{BASE}/bots/new")
  puts "new page: #{browser.current_url}"
  puts "NEW  => #{switch_state(browser).inspect}"

  # Click the visible label text, as a person would.
  browser.at_xpath("//span[normalize-space(text())='Add to all open rooms']").click
  puts "NEW after clicking the label text => #{switch_state(browser).inspect}"

  browser.at_css("input[name='bot[name]']").type("Ops Bot")
  browser.at_css("form button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  puts "after create: #{browser.current_url}"
  puts "bots page has Ops Bot: #{browser.body.include?("Ops Bot")}"

  # Edit it: the switch should be on, and turning it off should save as off.
  browser.goto("#{BASE}/bots")
  edit_href = browser.evaluate("document.querySelector(\"a[aria-label^='Edit Ops Bot']\").getAttribute('href')")
  browser.goto("#{BASE}#{edit_href}")
  puts "EDIT => #{switch_state(browser).inspect}"
  browser.at_xpath("//span[normalize-space(text())='Add to all open rooms']").click
  puts "EDIT after clicking off => #{switch_state(browser).inspect}"
  browser.at_css("form button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  puts "after update: #{browser.current_url}"
ensure
  browser.quit
end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "## Open rooms

Bots don't join open rooms by default. People do: every active person is in every open room, and that doesn't change.
A bot is in an open room only if its author turned on **Add to all open rooms** on the bot form, which is a switch
(`users.add_to_all_open_rooms`, off by default).

- **Switch on:** the bot joins every open room that exists at that moment. This happens in `Bot#join_open_rooms`,
  from an `after_save` that only fires when the value changes, so saving the form again doesn't re-run it.
- **Rooms that appear later:** `Rooms::Open` grants a new open room to `User.joining_open_rooms`: every active person,
  plus the bots with the switch on. A closed room that becomes open gets the same grant, so it covers both new rooms
  and rooms converted to open.
- **Switch off:** the flag is cleared, but nothing else changes. The bot keeps every membership it has. There's no
  bulk leave.
- **Closed rooms** aren't affected by the switch. A bot gets into one only when a person picks it in the room form.
- **Deleting** a bot clears the switch along with its code and webhook.

Why a flag and not a one-off join: a switch that's on has to keep covering rooms created later, so the setting
has to be stored. The column lives on `users` because `Bot < User` is single-table inheritance. Only bots read it,
and it's false for everyone else.

## Posting API
"
}

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "### Joins

When a bot is added to a room, its webhook receives a `joined` event, once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/<bot-code>/messages" }
}
```

The payload has no author, message or body. The room is the same `room` object as in a mention, so the bot can
post into it straight away with `reply_to`, or answer in the response, the same as for a mention.

- **Which joins count:** any time a bot gains a membership in a room that isn't a direct room. A person causes it
  by creating or revising a closed room with the bot picked. Campfire causes it automatically when the switch is
  turned on, when a new open room is created, or when a closed room becomes open.
- **Once per room:** a bot is announced only for memberships that were actually created. Granting a bot a room it's
  already in, or turning the switch on again, doesn't announce it again. A bot that leaves a room and is added back is
  a new join, so it's announced again.
- **Direct rooms never announce.** A direct conversation is private, so a bot never learns about it.
- **Bots without a webhook** aren't announced, since there's nowhere to send the event.
- **Queued after commit:** the event is enqueued after the surrounding transaction commits, so the webhook sees the
  membership when it runs. `Room::Memberships#grant_to` reports which memberships it created, using
  `insert_all(..., returning:)`. Only those rows are announced.
- **Removed before it runs:** `Bot::Webhook` checks the bot is still a member, active and has its webhook. A bot that
  has left the room isn't called, and a deactivated bot isn't called either.

**Every way a person or an automatic rule puts a bot in a room must go through `Room::Memberships#grant_to`.**
A membership written any other way, such as `Membership.create!`, has no callback, so it doesn't announce the bot.
In the app today every join goes through `grant_to`: `Room.create_for`, `revise` (the room forms), `Rooms::Open`
and `Bot#join_open_rooms`. The webhook tests set up a bot with `memberships.create!`, so they don't see a `joined`
event, and they're about mentions.

### Limits and safety
"
}

messages.content:
The work is complete. The full suite passes (432 runs, 0 failures, 22 skips that were already there), rubocop is clean, and brakeman reports no warnings.

## What changed

**Data.** A migration adds `users.add_to_all_open_rooms` (boolean, default false). Bots are `users` rows, so the flag lives there.

**Open rooms.** Bots no longer join open rooms when they're created.
- **Switch on:** `Bot` joins every open room that exists at that moment.
- **Rooms created later:** new open rooms, and closed rooms that become open, grant membership to `User.joining_open_rooms`: active people plus bots with the switch on.
- **Switch off:** clears the flag and keeps every current membership.
- **Deactivating a bot:** also clears the flag.

**`joined` events.** All grants now go through `Room::Memberships#grant_to`, which uses `insert_all ... returning:` to find the memberships it actually created. Each bot among them, in a non-direct room and with a webhook, gets one `Bot::WebhookJob`. The job is enqueued after the transaction commits, so the webhook sees the membership. Already-present members are not announced again.
- **Payload:** `{"event":"joined","room":{id,name,reply_to}}`, with no other keys.
- **Replies:** a 200 text or HTML reply is posted into the room, the same as for `mention`.
- **Direct rooms** never announce.

**Bot form.** The "Add to all open rooms" switch is a real checkbox inside a `<label>`, using the existing `.switch` styling. It's off by default, and its hint says what it does. The webhook hint now mentions joins.

**Open-room form.** The member list now shows only people and bots with the switch on. Before, it marked every active user as having access.

## Tests and docs
- I updated two existing tests that asserted the old default. One was the "creating a bot grants open rooms" test. The other was an autocomplete test that relied on auto-join.
- New tests cover the open-room policy, join events (once per room, direct rooms, commit timing), the `joined` payload and replies, the form, and the closed-room and open-room forms.
- `docs/bots.md` documents the open-room rules, the `joined` event, and the known gaps.

## Browser check
The system tests can't run here because there's no chromedriver. Instead I ran a throwaway development server and drove the real Chromium through Ferrum. I signed in, and checked that the switch is an unchecked checkbox nested in its label. Clicking the visible text toggled it. Creating a bot with the switch on worked, and the edit page showed it persisted. Turning it off saved, and the database kept the bot's membership. I then removed the development database.

## Decisions to review
- **Re-adding counts as a new join.** A bot removed from a room and added back gets `joined` again. I read "exactly once per room" as once per membership. I documented this as a choice.
- **Plain `memberships.create!` doesn't announce.** There's no callback, so every app join path has to go through `grant_to`. I documented this as a rule. The existing webhook tests use `create!`, so they're unaffected.
- **Existing bots keep their current open-room memberships.** I didn't add a data migration, since the bot feature is unreleased in this repo.
